Use appearance=analysis, brief or ledger for a full plot, a source-summary composition or a plot-and-values comparison. Supply an explicitly labelled summary for Brief; missing observations are excluded from observed totals, not treated as zero.
Keep the data table available for exact values and assistive technology.
accessibility: Provide a caption and description that explain the data.
The keyboard inspector and optional data table expose values without relying on color or hover.

bar-chart.description: Compare series with grouped, stacked or horizontal bars and a shared interactive tooltip.
usage: Pass a stable data array and meaningful series labels.
Keep variant=grouped, stacked or horizontal for the plot geometry; all three remain in the Chart mode control.
Use appearance=analysis to compare series, brief to lead with a labelled source measure, or ledger for adjacent exact values. Never add geometry-changing decoration to the marks.
Keep the data table available for exact values and assistive technology.
accessibility: Provide a caption and description that explain the data.
The keyboard inspector and optional data table expose values without relying on color or hover.

line-chart.description: Track changes using linear, smooth or step lines with accessible point inspection.
usage: Pass a stable data array and meaningful series labels.
Keep variant=linear, smooth or step in the independent Chart mode control. Missing observations remain disconnected even when interpolation is enabled.

Use appearance=analysis for trend comparison, brief to foreground the explicitly labelled latest observation, or ledger to read the curve beside its values. A missing final observation must not silently become an earlier value.
Keep the data table available for exact values and assistive technology.
accessibility: Provide a caption and description that explain the data.
The keyboard inspector and optional data table expose values without relying on color or hover.

pie-chart.description: Show proportions using themed pie and donut layouts, with readable totals and segment inspection.
usage: Pass a stable data array and meaningful series labels.
Keep variant=pie or donut in the independent Chart mode control. Shares are derived from finite positive values; an all-zero dataset is not a fabricated full slice.

Use appearance=analysis for a share disc, brief to lead with an explicitly labelled source total, or ledger to keep contribution values alongside the graphic. Legend filters do not change an explicitly supplied source-summary total.
Keep the data table available for exact values and assistive technology.
accessibility: Provide a caption and description that explain the data.
The keyboard inspector and optional data table expose values without relying on color or hover.

radar-chart.description: Compare several dimensions with a shared radar scale and contextual series highlighting.
usage: Pass a stable data array and meaningful series labels.

Keep variant=polygon, rounded or grid in the independent Chart mode control. Keep a shared maximum across profiles; missing axes break the path and remove its fill rather than becoming zero-valued vertices.
Use appearance=analysis for profile comparison, brief for an explicitly labelled source measure, or ledger for legible companion values. The sample mean names how many observations it includes.
Keep the data table available for exact values and assistive technology.
accessibility: Provide a caption and description that explain the data.
The keyboard inspector and optional data table expose values without relying on color or hover.

radial-chart.description: Show progress against a shared maximum using full rings or semicircles.
usage: Pass a stable data array and meaningful series labels.
Keep variant=full or semicircle in the independent Chart mode control. Each goal is measured against max; independent goal percentages must not be added into a shared total.
Use appearance=analysis for independent goals, brief to foreground one named goal, or ledger to compare exact values. The sample Brief explicitly labels Weekly review and its target of100.
Keep the data table available for exact values and assistive technology.
accessibility: Provide a caption and description that explain the data.
The keyboard inspector and optional data table expose values without relying on color or hover.

chart-tooltip.description: Compare a point, read its known subtotal or rank its series. Values update in place and keep their series colours.
usage: Pass an active point with meaningful labels and optional null observations. Position and bounds are local to the chart plot.
Use presentation compare, summary or ranked. Summary labels incomplete data as a known subtotal; missing observations are never counted as zero.

Keep the data table available for exact values and assistive technology. The noninteractive tooltip bounds its visible rows rather than adding an unusable scrollbar; remaining values stay in assistive text.
Point changes preserve matching row nodes and colours. The example supports focus, arrows, Home/End and Escape without relying on hover.
accessibility: Provide a caption and description that explain the data.
The keyboard inspector and optional data table expose values without relying on color or hover.

item-adornment.description: Coloured organic shapes for list items, with deterministic automatic selection and custom icon or no-icon options.
usage: Menu and select items default to a single stable icon. Direct ItemAdornment use can combine an icon and background when that composition is appropriate.
Pass adornment={false} or "none" to hide it, {shape,color} to choose a shape and tone, or a React element for your own icon.
Use ItemAdornment directly in your own lists. Meaningful state must also have a text or semantic label.
Within an adornment object, set showIcon or showBackground independently. Both false hides both; custom React icons and adornment={false} still work.
accessibility: Decorative adornments are hidden from assistive technology.
Text labels remain the accessible item names; selection does not depend on colour alone.

appearance.description: Choose from six coordinated palettes and adjust reading contrast across the application.
usage: Mount AppearanceProvider once around your application. AppearanceMenu or AppearanceControls changes the shared appearance.
Palettes and contrast persist in local storage. Controlled value/onValueChange is available for your own settings surface.
Contrast adjusts semantic text and edges; it does not filter artwork or alter accent fills.
accessibility: Text role pairs retain at least 4.5:1 on primary surfaces at every setting. Control edges retain 3:1.
The contrast slider supports keyboard arrows, Home and End. Palette changes apply to portalled controls too.

scroll-organism.description: A softly stretching companion driven by native document scrolling.
usage: Position the decorative organism at the edge of a scrolling story. Tune shape, size and travel.
It uses Motion values without per-frame React renders or scroll interception.
accessibility: The decorative organism is hidden from assistive technology and ignores pointer events.
Motion Off and reduced motion keep it still.

assembly-part.description: A persistent native component moving between a floating organism and its measured layout.
usage: Use this primitive inside a measured composition. Preserve stable part identity while target geometry changes.
asChild retains the native interactive element. Assembly controls manage its interactivity during travel.
accessibility: Settled parts retain native keyboard behaviour. Moving parts are inert until placed.

organism-composition.description: Six useful compositions made from persistent Cojeev base components, with organic assembly and native controls.
usage: Choose profile, side-panel, dock, chat, focus or invite. Each layout uses the actual library primitives.
Use assembled={false} for the floating state. Keep the component mounted to retain local state while changing kinds.
Focus uses a real local elapsed-time countdown. Invite records local RSVP state; provide callbacks for your application.
accessibility: Moving controls remain inert until arrival, then regain normal keyboard, hover and form behavior.
Motion Off and reduced motion produce usable, unclipped components immediately.

organism-assembly.description: An interactive studio that gathers floating shapes into six reusable compositions.
usage: Choose Profile, Panel, Dock, Chat, Focus or Invite. Replay scatters and reassembles their native parts.
Use value/onValueChange for a controlled chooser and compositionProps to configure the underlying composition.
accessibility: Arrow keys, Home and End navigate the chooser; the mobile grid keeps all six choices visible.
Motion Off and reduced motion keep controls immediately usable and disable replay.

focus-session.description: A local focus timer composed from Cojeev cards, progress, badges and native controls.
usage: Import FocusSession from the focus-session entry. Set durationSeconds (default 1500, bounded to 1–86400) and optional name or description.
Start, pause and reset the real local countdown. Changing duration resets the session; the example's 5, 15 and 25 minute choices each begin a fresh session.
Use onAction for start, pause, reset and complete events. OrganismProps also supports controlled state/onStateChange and assembly presentation.
The documentation timer is a local demo. It does not create a reminder, notification or saved task, and reloading clears its state.
accessibility: Native buttons support keyboard activation. Remaining time and progress stay available as readable values.
Reduced motion and global Off preserve the usable timer; decorative motion is independent of elapsed time.

invite-card.description: An event invitation with participant avatars and a reversible local RSVP, composed from Cojeev primitives.
usage: Import InviteCard from the invite-card entry. Set name, description, inviteDate, inviteTime and inviteLocation to describe the event.
Pass up to four participants as {name, initials}. The yes/no controls update the local rsvp state and emit onAction with action='rsvp' and value='yes' or 'no'.
Use controlled state/onStateChange when the response belongs to your application. Persistence and delivery remain the consumer's responsibility.
The documentation example is a fictional invitation. Its responses stay in the preview and send no invitation, email or calendar update.
accessibility: Event details are text; native RSVP buttons remain keyboard accessible and expose their current selection.
The quiet-motion settings preserve assembled, usable controls and readable invitation details.

profile-card.description: A reusable profile card composed from Cojeev base components.
usage: Use the standalone wrapper for an immediately usable composition.
Configure content and callbacks through its typed props; the same parts can be used in OrganismAssembly.
accessibility: Native buttons and inputs retain keyboard and form behaviour.
Local example feedback describes the performed demo action.

Configure content and callbacks through its typed props; the same parts can be used in OrganismAssembly.

Local example feedback describes the performed demo action.

hero-button.description: Twelve tactile calls to action: living ink, paper, keys, tickets and small moments of motion around one native button.
usage: Use shape="organic" or "capsule"; showArrow={false} removes the arrow.
Use asChild with one anchor for native link navigation. The button keeps loading, disabled and form semantics.

appearance selects liquid, split-arrow, paper-fold, pressed-key, ribbon, ticket, seal, ink-sweep, orbit, sliding-window, stacked-paper or spotlight. These change the silhouette, material detail or response; variant still selects the semantic surface and size remains independent.

Organic is the original liquid treatment; Capsule keeps its regular rim. Both remain in the gallery alongside the new concepts. Every example is live and reports local activations only. Copy code includes your current concept and size.
accessibility: Keyboard focus gives the same arrow feedback as hover.
Motion Off, Flow Off and reduced motion keep a static arrow and usable control.
Decoration is pointer-transparent and hidden from assistive technology. The sliding label is announced once. Hover moves paint, not the native hit target, and no concept runs an idle animation.

depth-background.description: Layered pollen, contours and orbital shapes with perspective, native-scroll depth and pointer response.
usage: Place inside a positioned section; the background fills its parent without intercepting clicks.
Choose a variant and stable seed. Tune density from 0.35 to 2 and intensity from 0 to 2; zero intensity keeps it still.
accessibility: Decorative, hidden from assistive technology and never focusable.
Offscreen, hidden-page and reduced-motion states stop its movement. Keep text on a readable foreground.

float-layer.description: An entrance, scroll depth and gentle idle movement for a real component or a group of elements.
usage: Set depth and drift in pixels. Use depth={0} drift={0} for a stationary foreground after its entrance; reserve idle drift and parallax for background layers.
Tune revealDuration (0.2–2 seconds), revealDistance (0–80 pixels) and delay. Set replay to reveal again whenever the layer re-enters the viewport.
The default wrapper keeps transforms separate. asChild preserves the child element; use the wrapper when that child owns an inline CSS translate.
accessibility: Server-rendered content stays readable before hydration.
Reduced motion and Motion Off leave content visible and still; offscreen and hidden-page work pauses.

shape-artwork.description: An original SVG silhouette with a cast shadow and a rotated rear outline. The same vector layers power its live preview and standalone SVG export.
usage: Set name to one of the 12 signature shapes; choose pink, olive, blue or yellow with tone. Set rotation in degrees and filled={false} for an outlined foreground.
Use shadow and echo to toggle the cast shadow and rear outline. shadowAngle sets the cast direction clockwise from the right; echoAngle rotates the rear outline relative to the foreground.

shapeArtworkSvg(options, colors?) returns an original standalone SVG string; supply resolved fill, shadow and echo colors to preserve a customized palette. Its fixed viewBox contains every supported shape at all layer angles.

shapeArtworkCode(options) returns a React usage snippet containing every selected prop. The landing workbench downloads a transparent SVG and provides accessible copying with visible success or failure feedback.

Optional ambient={true} breathes between name and a compatible morphTo contour; morphDuration is a full4–20 second cycle and motionDelay is clamped to0–3 seconds. Omit ambient for a still shape. The shared studio exposes these settings and shapeArtworkCode includes them. Rotation/layer changes are immediate; Motion Off and reduced motion settle to the rest contour.
accessibility: The SVG is decorative by default. Supply label when the graphic conveys meaning; native SVG props and refs are forwarded.
Motion Off, Flow Off, reduced motion and hidden or offscreen rendering settle the contour immediately.
The example changes local artwork settings only. Export is vector artwork, with the selected target contour rather than a transient animation frame.

word-relay.description: Exchanges phrases, words or letters inside a stable wrapping footprint, with interruptible motion and explicit navigation.
usage: Pass words and optionally control index/onIndexChange. All candidates share one wrapping layout footprint, so the surrounding content stays in place.

Choose split="phrase" (default), "word" or "grapheme". staggerFrom="first", "last", "center" or "edges" sets the logical arrival order; direction="up" or "down" sets travel. Stagger is milliseconds, evenly bounded to a 500ms window.

Automatic changes are opt-in through auto; pair with a pause control. interval is 1200–60000ms and always allows the transition plus at least 500ms at rest. duration is 0–1600ms. loop=false stops at the last phrase.

Use controlsRef for next(), previous(), jumpTo(index) and reset(). The normal ref still returns the span. Controlled navigation requests onIndexChange; the parent must apply the new index. reset returns to defaultIndex.
Use tone="inherit" inside a heading, or a native accent tone for an organic highlight.
accessibility: Only the current phrase is exposed to assistive technology; animated layers are hidden. Add aria-live only if the content warrants announcements.
Hover and focus pause automatic playback. Reduced motion, shared Motion Off, Flow Off, hidden tabs and offscreen content suspend the timer.
Empty words produce an empty span, and out-of-range indexes clamp to the available phrases.
Grapheme grouping preserves emoji and combining marks; use word or phrase grouping to preserve joining in scripts such as Arabic.

reading-trail.description: Keep your place with a connected spine, an expandable bookmark or a descriptive chapter overview—all following actual reading progress.
usage: Pass items with existing document IDs and readable labels. Native anchors remain available before JavaScript.
Use scrollRoot for a contained scrolling panel. The default tracks the document; offset sets the current-section activation line.
Duplicate IDs are consolidated. Missing sections do not claim measured progress.
Optional presentation chooses spine, bookmark or overview. Omission preserves the original document TOC. Item descriptions support a useful chapter preview, not a second navigation label.
Bookmark keeps the current chapter, previous/next and an expandable contents list. Escape closes the contents and restores its trigger. Presentation changes retain the article and scroll position.
The example article uses the shared organic ScrollArea. Native links stay stationary; only the marker and underline paint respond.
accessibility: Links preserve modifier clicks and normal URLs. A selected destination receives focus.
Current section is exposed through aria-current. Optional smooth scrolling respects shared quiet settings.

living-link.description: A native link with a drawn ink contour, directional underline reveals, or an organic pigment wash.
usage: Pass href and normal anchor attributes. direction can be forward or up-right.
Use disabled to keep an announced, unavailable label without a navigable URL.
treatment selects contour (the original resting mark), underline-start, underline-end, underline-center, wash-up or wash-across. Start/end follow the reading direction.
tone selects pink, olive, blue or yellow for a restrained wash; text keeps its theme ink throughout the transition. Arrows exchange through a small window in the five new treatments.
accessibility: Native link navigation, modifier clicks and keyboard activation remain intact.
Hover and focus share the same emphasis. Disabled anchors leave the tab order. Reduced motion keeps a still, readable underline.

pigment-field.description: An original GPU pigment wash using the current Cojeev palette.
usage: Place inside a positioned parent with a height. Keep meaningful content in a sibling above the decorative field.
Control tone, speed (0–3), intensity (0–2) and paused. The canvas caps pixel density and responds to resizing.
This background is an original shader foundation; it does not yet implement pointer-fluid refraction over HTML.
Place text on an opaque native Card or other readable surface over the changing artwork; do not assume contrast against every shader pixel.
accessibility: Decorative canvas is inert, hidden from assistive technology and never captures pointer events.
Reduced motion, offscreen content, document visibility and shared Motion/Flow Off suspend continuous rendering. A static fallback covers unavailable or lost contexts.

contour-field.description: Original topographic lines on the inherited paper surface, with a bounded GPU renderer.
usage: Place inside a positioned parent with a height. Keep content outside the decorative field.
Control tone, speed (0–3), intensity (0–2) and paused. A still fallback is available when GPU rendering cannot run.
Use an opaque native surface for meaningful text placed above the changing artwork.
accessibility: The field is decorative, inert and ignores pointer hit testing.
Animation suspends with reduced motion, shared quiet settings, hidden tabs and offscreen content.

milestone-path.description: Follow caller-owned progress as a connected Journey, a scrollable Sequence or a compact checkpoint Review.
usage: Pass stable IDs and explicit complete, current or upcoming states. Supply title, description and metadata for context.

Set presentation to journey, sequence or review; omit it to keep the original vertical composition. Sequence uses the shared organic horizontal scrollbar and native keyboard/pointer scrolling. Every presentation keeps descriptions and explicit status text.

The example retains progress and selected detail across layout changes. Selecting a title opens local detail; only the separate completion action advances the sample. Current-marker contour motion stays off the native44px title target.
Provide onMilestoneSelect only when a milestone has a real action. Noninteractive milestones remain ordinary content.
MilestonePath composes the existing Stepper parts. The caller owns explicit states; it does not invent a separate selected-row model.
accessibility: Progress state is named in text as well as color. Buttons retain native keyboard and disabled behavior.
The ordered sequence remains meaningful with motion disabled or without an interactive action.

activity-feed.description: An ordered, date-grouped history with a quiet connecting margin, readable actors and timestamps, and updates that keep your place.
usage: Pass entries in the order they should appear, with stable IDs and optional actor, timestamp, badge and details.
Provide group labels for visible consecutive date sections and dateTime for machine-readable timestamps. Labels and chronology remain caller-owned; the feed never interprets text such as Today.

New entries inserted before the existing first entry extend a limited view so already-visible updates and their mounted state remain. Appended older history still waits for Show more. Stable IDs are required.
Omit initialVisible to show all supplied entries. Set initialVisible and pageSize to reveal supplied history in pages.
The feed displays your data; it does not fetch, manufacture events or reorder timestamps.
accessibility: A semantic ordered list preserves chronology. Show more announces the new count and moves focus to the first newly shown entry.
Images are decorative alongside named actors. New content respects the shared reduced-motion contract.

text-ribbon.description: A measured phrase follows six original SVG paths, with direct manipulation and gentle changes of pace.
usage: Choose circle, loop, wave, arch, line or figure-eight. Circle has a compact square artwork; the other paths scale from a 640 × 280 viewBox.
Automatic motion is opt-in with auto. Supply a visible pause control via paused. Speed is bounded to 0–120 SVG units per second; fontSize is bounded to 24–56.
Use a short decorative phrase. The visual path repeats it, while assistive technology reads the text once. Use guide and tone to show a simple path or a native accent stroke.
Set curvature from 0 to 1 for the arch and wave. Choose hoverBehavior=pause, slow, quicken or none; pace changes ease continuously.
draggable adds direct horizontal manipulation, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and Home. Vertical touch gestures preserve scrolling. Automatic movement is still opt-in.
Omit direction for local direction after a drag, or supply direction/onDirectionChange to own it. Paused and quiet settings stop automatic travel while explicit positioning remains available.
accessibility: Keep critical prose in ordinary readable text. A curved ribbon works best as an optional expressive detail.

Focus pauses movement. Hover pauses by default; slow and quicken are optional. Reduced motion, local data-flow=off, data-no-glide, shared Motion Off, Flow Off, hidden documents and offscreen views suspend automatic travel.
The SVG is hidden from assistive technology. The complete supplied phrase remains in the accessible DOM, including when motion is disabled.

glyph-sculpture.description: A real 3D surface drawn with glyphs, optional contour marks and your own local geometry.
usage: Choose glyphSet="density", "digits" or "letters". edgeMatching adds contour-direction marks to density glyphs; cellSize is bounded to 7–20px.
Pass form="bloom", "seed" or "pebble", or supply immutable geometry with positions, optional triangles and normals. Invalid geometry reports onGeometryError and keeps a built-in form.
Use turn, pitch and zoom for explicit orientation; wrap with SculptureOrbit for native drag, keyboard, zoom and reset controls. Pausing optional motion does not disable direct orientation changes.

loadSculptureFile accepts local self-contained GLB, filled SVG, PNG or JPEG up to 8 MiB. Image limits are 4 million pixels. Images become luminance reliefs; imported materials are replaced by the selected native ink tone. Imports never upload the file.
Use paused or speed=0 for a still sculpture. Decorative rendering stops while offscreen, hidden, reduced-motion, Flow Off or Motion Off.
accessibility: The rendered sculpture is decorative. Put any essential information in adjacent readable text and native controls.
SculptureOrbit supplies labelled keyboard controls; optional hover tracking has no essential action.
A static fallback remains when Canvas2D is unavailable. Failed local imports report an actionable message and retain the previous sculpture.

dither-sculpture.description: Depth-tested sculptural forms printed as ordered dots, halftone, error diffusion or stipple.
usage: Choose pattern="ordered", "halftone", "diffusion" or "stipple". grainSize is 1.5–9px and density is 0.5–1.6. Patterns respond to actual surface lighting and depth.
Pass form="bloom", "seed" or "pebble", or supply immutable geometry with positions, optional triangles and normals. Invalid geometry reports onGeometryError and keeps a built-in form.
Use turn, pitch and zoom for explicit orientation; wrap with SculptureOrbit for native drag, keyboard, zoom and reset controls. Pausing optional motion does not disable direct orientation changes.

loadSculptureFile accepts local self-contained GLB, filled SVG, PNG or JPEG up to 8 MiB. Image limits are 4 million pixels. Images become luminance reliefs; imported materials are replaced by the selected native ink tone. Imports never upload the file.
Use paused or speed=0 for a still sculpture. Decorative rendering stops while offscreen, hidden, reduced-motion, Flow Off or Motion Off.
accessibility: The rendered sculpture is decorative. Put any essential information in adjacent readable text and native controls.
SculptureOrbit supplies labelled keyboard controls; optional hover tracking has no essential action.
A static fallback remains when Canvas2D is unavailable. Failed local imports report an actionable message and retain the previous sculpture.

ink-sculpture.description: Hatched and engraved marks follow the light and relief of a 3D form.
usage: Choose treatment="hatch", "crosshatch" or "contour". markSize is 4–16px, density is 0.5–1.6, angle is ±180°, and relief is 0–1.
Pass form="bloom", "seed" or "pebble", or supply immutable geometry with positions, optional triangles and normals. Invalid geometry reports onGeometryError and keeps a built-in form.

semantic-bloom.description: A living wordmark whose particles wander, connect and gather into a liquid organism. Adapted from ThreeUI with Cojeev colors and motion controls.
